Thanks for the quick demo earlier — NextEra Diagnostics is very interested in Redwood for our clinical decision-support assistant. Can you provide: 1) a short DPA addendum or language we can sign that confirms no training; 2) a CSV or document listing subprocessors, their regions, and whether they have access to prompt/response content; and 3) any evidence or artifacts (SOC2, contractual clauses) that show controls around model improvement opt-outs?

We're aiming to complete legal review by next week.

From: Elena Ortiz <e.ortiz@nextera-dx.com>

Subject: Re: DPA addendum draft and evidence

Rishi — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying questions after a first pass:
1) The draft references "Redwood-managed telemetry" — can you confirm whether any unredacted prompt/response pairs ever leave the tenant boundary for internal troubleshooting? NextEra requires that such content never be accessible to human reviewers without explicit customer authorization.
2) Subprocessors CSV: does it include any cloud providers or inference engine partners who may have access to KV caches or model weights? We need to understand if any third parties have low-level access that could make reconstruction of prompts possible.
3) Cross-border transfers: we need a short statement about whether Redwood or any subprocessors transfer inference logs outside of the US (we have EU-based clinics). If so, what safeguards (SCCs, standard contractual clauses) or regional isolation options exist?

If you can provide quick written confirmations on the three items, procurement can proceed to generate a PO and route the addendum to our legal team.

Thanks,
Elena

From: ava_chen@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ortiz <e.ortiz@nextera-dx.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum draft and evidence — operational controls summary

Elena — quick operational confirmations below:

1) Human access to prompt/response content: Redwood's standard practice is that unredacted prompts/responses are tenant-isolated. Engineering and support personnel do not have access to raw prompt/response pairs by default. For debugging, developers can request logs through a ticket; such requests require customer authorization or are limited to redacted/hashed records. We will add mandatory customer approval language to the addendum to reflect this.

2) Subprocessors: the attached CSV lists cloud providers, telemetry pipelines, and a managed inference partner used for specialized accelerators. None of the listed subprocessors have direct access to model weights; they operate at the infrastructure layer. We will also provide a short column indicating whether the subprocessor processes prompt/response content and the legal basis.

3) Cross-border transfers: Redwood performs regional routing by default. We operate US and EU regions; inference logs for EU customers can be kept in-region on request. Where transfers occur (e.g., cross-region failover), SCCs are in place for applicable subprocessors and we can include a cross-border transfer statement in the addendum.

I'll update the CSV with the processing columns and send an annotated export by EOD.

- Ava
Product Policy Manager | Redwood Inference
